faq.a: Hauwau is associated with the Arabic form حَوَّاء, whose core sense is hauwau; eve (hausa form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Hauwau?
faq.a: Hauwau is associated with Arabic. Hauwau is the Hausa form of Arabic حَوَّاء (Ḥawwāʾ), the name of Eve.
Yes — the underlying form حَوَّاء is Arabic.
Hauwau can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hauwau should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ḥawwāʾ is not a Quranic personal name, though Eve is referred to in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Hauwau mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Hauwau is rendered حوا and carries the sense حوا، حضرت حوا.

faq.q: What does Hauwau mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hauwau is rendered حوا and carries the sense حوا، حوا.
A romanized syllable approximation is hau-wau. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Hauwau?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Hauwau, hauwau. Script forms are حوا, حَوَّاء, हव्वा.

faq.q: Is Hauwau a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
